newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel Corp falls as family feud looms.
newsitem.headline: Israel Corp falls as family feud looms.

text.p: Israel Corp shares fell sharply on Sunday on media reports the company would lie at the centre of a burgeoning family feud for control of the international empire of the late billionaire Shoul Eisenberg.
Israel Corp fell 6.25 percent to 209.36 shekels. Israel Chemicals, 41.9 percent of which is held by Israel Corp, fell by three percent to 4.04 shekels.
"There is an inheritance battle and it is not clear who will end up managing the company," Ron Weisberg of IBI Investments told Reuters.
Media reports broke last week of a looming dispute between Eisenberg's son Erwin, who inherited 80 percent of the Eisenberg empire, and widow Leah Eisenberg.

Israel's media on Sunday carried a blow-by-blow account of the family quarrel, Israel's biggest inheritance battle. Media reports said Eisenberg's widow claimed Israeli family law entitled her to half of her husband's empire.

A spokesman and the lawyer for Erwin Eisenberg, who was named chairman of Israel Corp and Israel Chemicals in April, refused comment on the dispute. Leah Eisenberg's attorney was unavailable for comment.
Israel Corp is one of Israel's major holding companies with investments in more than 80 leading firms. Company founder Shoul Eisenberg died of a heart attack in Beijing in March.

The Eisenberg Group is involved in international projects in iron and steel, electricity generation, utilities, cement, edible oils, chemicals, textiles, shipbuilding, agriculture and water management.
The company is also active in the trade of fertilisers, steel, chemicals, tools and textiles and is involved in aircraft trading and leasing.
Israel Corp is the main vehicle for the Eisenberg Group's Israeli investments.
